Tips for Alice (Cardinal, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a track can't tell protection from framing or the Katana. But if a trusted Lookout names X as the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 11 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads and explain any switch before the vote. A read/vote mismatch is only a lead: never shoot or hang on it alone. (seen in 9 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat unless a full census proves otherwise, and the Katana holder reads Good that night. (seen in 8 games)
- Unless a Clerk may have an unused rig, treat nomination and trial as separate votes. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) needs a test, not an automatic acquittal. (seen in 10 games)
- Put every result, and tonight's labeled plan, in your will each Day. Post results that matter publicly too, since a Mortician can hide wills. (seen in 6 games)

## Village
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. Players who DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new info are a likely Yakuza bloc. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No or Innocent with them, argued to delay, or exchanged PMs with them. A Guilty vote clears nobody, since it may be a bus. Demand a claim before hanging. (seen in 11 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name another living player's exact role; say 'ask X'. (seen in 11 games)
- Never announce tonight's investigation or protection target, publicly or by PM. It tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 7 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, do slot math daily. A claim that duplicates a role listed once, or that overflows the unseen slots, marks a liar, and a late lone Vanilla is often the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 4 games)
- If a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among that side's voters. Recompute the threshold, then pick out the stuffer by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty). If your Innocents plus a Ballot Stuffer can save them, defend them. Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later. (seen in 14 games)
- Fake roles whose tokens match yours (an Accountant may audit you), and never a role a living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict. Don't switch claims once broken. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game. (seen in 8 games)
- Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit. Avoid hitting confident unclaimed organizers, who may be alerting Veterans. (seen in 7 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retry, or hang the defended Neutral. (seen in 8 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder and target every night; with two left, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout could have seen. Agree a cover in night chat and admit the visit at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Feed exact-role info (Diviner, Mortician, claims) into Ritualist guesses for certain kills, alongside the Katana. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked; nobody else knows the target. If you must explain, pick one claim and never switch. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 6 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat. (seen in 11 games)

## Eavesdropper
- Pick a target who will survive and send PMs, such as the Day 1 PM-cluster starter. An empty record clears nobody. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard vocal analysts and claimed investigators. Once you're claimed, spend a token to self-protect instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 10 games)
- You get no save feedback; say only that a survival is consistent with your protection. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check on an unverifiable claim, flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners), never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; every waiting night lets the town hang you first. (seen in 3 games)

- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, do slot math daily. A claim that duplicates a role listed once, or that overflows the unseen slots, marks a liar, and a late lone Vanilla is often the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 4 games)
- If a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among that side's voters. Recompute the threshold, then pick out the stuffer by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty). If your Innocents plus a Ballot Stuffer can save them, defend them. Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later. (seen in 14 games)
- Fake roles whose tokens match yours (an Accountant may audit you), and never a role a living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict. Don't switch claims once broken. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game. (seen in 8 games)
- Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit. Avoid hitting confident unclaimed organizers, who may be alerting Veterans. (seen in 7 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retry, or hang the defended Neutral. (seen in 8 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder and target every night; with two left, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout could have seen. Agree a cover in night chat and admit the visit at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Feed exact-role info (Diviner, Mortician, claims) into Ritualist guesses for certain kills, alongside the Katana. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked; nobody else knows the target. If you must explain, pick one claim and never switch. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 6 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat. (seen in 11 games)

- Pick a target who will survive and send PMs, such as the Day 1 PM-cluster starter. An empty record clears nobody. (seen in 3 games)

- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard vocal analysts and claimed investigators. Once you're claimed, spend a token to self-protect instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 10 games)

- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check on an unverifiable claim, flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners), never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed. (seen in 5 games)

- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads and explain any switch before the vote. A read/vote mismatch is only a lead: never shoot or hang on it alone. (seen in 9 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat unless a full census proves otherwise, and the Katana holder reads Good that night. (seen in 8 games)
- Unless a Clerk may have an unused rig, treat nomination and trial as separate votes. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) needs a test, not an automatic acquittal. (seen in 10 games)
- Put every result, and tonight's labeled plan, in your will each Day. Post results that matter publicly too, since a Mortician can hide wills. (seen in 6 games)

## Village
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. Players who DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new info are a likely Yakuza bloc. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No or Innocent with them, argued to delay, or exchanged PMs with them. A Guilty vote clears nobody, since it may be a bus. Demand a claim before hanging. (seen in 11 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name another living player's exact role; say 'ask X'. (seen in 11 games)
- Never announce tonight's investigation or protection target, publicly or by PM. It tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 7 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, do slot math daily. A claim that duplicates a role listed once, or that overflows the unseen slots, marks a liar, and a late lone Vanilla is often the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 4 games)
- If a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among that side's voters. Recompute the threshold, then pick out the stuffer by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty). If your Innocents plus a Ballot Stuffer can save them, defend them. Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later. (seen in 14 games)
- Fake roles whose tokens match yours (an Accountant may audit you), and never a role a living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict. Don't switch claims once broken. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game. (seen in 8 games)
- Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit. Avoid hitting confident unclaimed organizers, who may be alerting Veterans. (seen in 7 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retry, or hang the defended Neutral. (seen in 8 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder and target every night; with two left, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout could have seen. Agree a cover in night chat and admit the visit at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Feed exact-role info (Diviner, Mortician, claims) into Ritualist guesses for certain kills, alongside the Katana. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked; nobody else knows the target. If you must explain, pick one claim and never switch. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 6 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat. (seen in 11 games)

## Eavesdropper
- Pick a target who will survive and send PMs, such as the Day 1 PM-cluster starter. An empty record clears nobody. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard vocal analysts and claimed investigators. Once you're claimed, spend a token to self-protect instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 10 games)
- You get no save feedback; say only that a survival is consistent with your protection. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check on an unverifiable claim, flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners), never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; every waiting night lets the town hang you first. (seen in 3 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 1, round 7 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.90; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 7, 3.00x; next round 3.50x):
   10 words: public 3.51, private 0.88
   25 words: public 4.30, private 1.07
   50 words: public 5.69, private 1.42
  100 words: public 8.75, private 2.19
  200 words: public 16.00, private 4.00
  400 words: public 35.00, private 8.75
  800 words: public 91.00, private 22.75
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 1, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 8.00; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 8, 3.50x; next round 4.00x):
   10 words: public 4.09, private 1.02
   25 words: public 5.01, private 1.25
   50 words: public 6.64, private 1.66
  100 words: public 10.21, private 2.55
  200 words: public 18.67, private 4.67
  400 words: public 40.83, private 10.21
  800 words: public 106.17, private 26.54
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 6.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 8.00; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 8, 3.50x; next round 4.00x):
   10 words: public 4.09, private 1.02
   25 words: public 5.01, private 1.25
   50 words: public 6.64, private 1.66
  100 words: public 10.21, private 2.55
  200 words: public 18.67, private 4.67
  400 words: public 40.83, private 10.21
  800 words: public 106.17, private 26.54
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 6.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33

It is Day 3, round 3 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.94; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices during this trial (1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58

Your public message this turn is free up to 150 words; beyond that you pay only for the extra length.
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

Task prompt
It is Day 4, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.34; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.
